name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 20, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at 5:00
p.m., on September 20, 2010, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 15, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:07 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

RECESS

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:02
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  September 20, 2010
 PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize OCFA Fire Paramedic/Captain Steve Concialdi for his Dedication to the
  Community Through his Youth Awareness Program in Orange County, "Friends
  Against Drinking and Driving"

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Captain Steve Concialdi.

P2.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Kelley presented certificates of commendation to Sergeant Oscar F. Mejia and
  Lance Corporal Jonathon D. Diehm.

P3.  Recognize the Mission Viejo Girls Softball 10 & Under District All Star Team
  "Adrenaline" for Placing 1st at the 2010 Western National Championships in
  Tucson Arizona

  Mayor Kelly presented commendations to the coaches and members of team Adrenaline.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Mazi Bahadori, M.V.: expressed concern that state law does not require disclosure of a
committee name or identification number on electronic campaign materials. He urged the City
Council to adopt a resolution requiring that all candidates and their affiliates list an ID number
on internet campaign materials.

Steven Guess, M.V.: reiterated the prior comments and expressed concern with the personal
attacks he read on the web site www.protectmissionviejo.com.

Larry Maurer, M.V.: speaking on behalf of the Friends of the Mission Viejo Library, he
discussed the upcoming Readers’ Festival and thanked Director of Library Services Valerie
Maginnis for her support and leadership.

Dave Rickett, M.V.: referring to the Planning Commission’s approval of an electronically
amplified electronic church bell system, he asked the City Council to reverse the decision.

Carl T. Raff, M.V.: expressed opposition to the city’s "grow house" ordinance. He stated that
the time is right for the city to consider where medical use of cannabis and the potential for
legalization will fit into the city’s long term plans.

John Maginnis, M.V.: announced that the library’s big, celebratory event will be held at the
Murray Center and Oso Viejo Park on Saturday, September 25, 2010, from 10:00 a.m. to 5:00
p.m. It is the only event of its kind in Orange County and he invited the Council Members and
residents to join the Friends of the Library at this year’s Readers’ Festival.

City Council Minutes  2  September 20, 2010
 Matt Corrigan, President of the Saddleback Republican Assembly, M.V.: announced that the
Saddleback Republican Assembly and the California Republican Assembly have endorsed
candidate Rhonda Reardon for City Council. Mr. Corrigan encouraged the Council to adopt a
revolving door ordinance as proposed by Council Member Schlicht at the September 7, 2010,
City Council Meeting.

Bari Russell, M.V.: asked why Santa’s Arrival and the workshop cannot be moved to the Murray
Community Center. She stated that it is inconvenient for library patrons to have the civic center
courtyard closed and she asked the City Council to consider moving the holiday event to the
Community Center next year.

Dennis O’Connor, M.V.: discussed political signs that are scattered throughout the community
and stated that there is no basis or fact behind the sign that says Mayor Kelley and Mayor Pro
Tem Leckness cannot be trusted. Mr. O’Connor stated that Trish Kelley is extremely dedicated
and the city is lucky to have her serving as its Mayor.

Dan Avery, M.V.: in response to Mr. Bahadori’s and Mr. Guess’ comments, he stated that he, as
a business owner, has every right to donate server space to the City Council candidates that he
supports.

Rick Sandzimier, M.V.: speaking as a resident and Chairman of the Planning Commission, he
announced that he had the privilege of sitting in on a Friends of the Mission Viejo Library Board
Meeting and he learned about many fantastic things that are going on behind the scenes.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 5, 6, and 18 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

3.  Check Register dated August 27, 2010, in the amount of $2,192,728.93

City Council Minutes  3  September 20, 2010
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated September 3, 2010, in the amount of $656,329.32

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  Quarterly Financial Report for the Community Development Agency (CDA) - For
  the Year Ended June 30, 2010 (Preliminary-Unaudited)

  Received and filed.

8.  Semi-Annual Financial Report for the Community Development Financing
  Authority (CDFA) - For the Year Ended June 30, 2010 (Preliminary-Unaudited)

  Received and filed.

9.  City Treasurer's Monthly Report for July 2010

  Received and filed.

10.  Community Development Agency (CDA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for July 2010

  Received and filed.

11.  Community Development Financing Authority (CDFA) Treasurer's Monthly
  Report for July 2010

  Received and filed.

12.  FY 2009-10 & FY 2010-11 Carryovers and Budget Amendments

  (1) Adopted Resolution 10-51 Amending the FY 2009-10 City Budget for Year-End
  Adjustments in Certain Accounts; and (2) adopted Resolution 10-52 Amending the FY
  2010-11 City Budget to Reflect Final Carryovers From FY 2009-10 and Certain Other
  Adjustments.

13.  FY 2009-10 & FY 2010-11 Carryovers and Budget Amendments for the Mission
  Viejo Community Development Agency (CDA)

  (1) Adopted CDA Resolution 10-06 of the Mission Viejo CDA Amending the FY 2009-
  10 Budget for Year-End Adjustments in Certain Accounts; and (2) adopted CDA
  Resolution 10-07 of the Mission Viejo CDA Amending the FY 2010-11 Budget to
  Reflect Final Carryovers from FY 2009-10.

City Council Minutes  4  September 20, 2010
 14.  City Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2009-10 and Annual Review of
  City’s Investment Policy

  (1) Received and filed the accompanying City Treasurer’s Annual Report for fiscal year
  2009-10; (2) adopted Resolution 10-53 Approving the City’s Investment Policy for FY
  2010-11; and (3) set the Benchmark Index for FY 2010-11 to be a Government Securities
  Index comprised of 60% three-month Treasury Bills; 25% Treasury and Agency
  securities with maturities greater than one year and up to three years; and 15% Treasury
  and Agency securities with maturities greater than three years and up to five years.

15.  Community Development Agency (CDA) Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal
  Year 2009-10 and Annual Review of the CDA Investment Policy

  (1) Received and filed the accompanying Treasurer’s Annual Report for fiscal year 2009-
  10; and (2) adopted CDA Resolution 10-08 Approving the CDA Investment Policy for
  FY 2010-11.

16.  Community Development Financing Authority (CDFA) Treasurer’s Annual Report
  for Fiscal Year 2009-10 and Annual Review of the CDFA Investment Policy

  (1) Received and filed the accompanying Treasurer’s Annual Report for fiscal year 2009-
  10; and (2) adopted CDFA Resolution 10-04 Approving the Authority’s Investment
  Policy for FY 2010-11.

17.  Various Speed Limit Updates Ordinance

  Adopted Ordinance 10-282 Amending Chapter 12.04.010(d) of the Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code Regarding Prima Facie Speed Limits on Certain Street.

19.  Ordinance update to Section 11.13.015 of Chapter 11.13 of Title 11 of the Mission
  Viejo Municipal Code Authorizing Professional Pest Control Providers to be Issued
  Animal Control Oriented Permits Without City Council Presentation

  Adopted Ordinance 10-284 Amending Section 11.13.015 of the Mission Viejo Municipal
  Code.

20.  California State Association of Counties (CSAC) Excess Insurance Authority

  Adopted Resolution 10-54 Delegating Authority to the City Manager or the Assistant
  City Manager to Act on Matters Relating to the CSAC Excess Insurance Authority.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

City Council Minutes  5  September 20, 2010
 NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht noted that the Minutes, on page 1, incorrectly reflect that
  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein was present
  on September 7 when in fact he was absent. She took issue with the City Attorney’s
  report of closed session on page 2 and clarified that he did not receive a 100% positive
  response as she believes that Mr. Curley should be released from his contract for legal
  services. On page 9, there is no indication that Mayor Pro Tem Leckness interrupted her
  Council Comments and on page 11, she objected to Trish Kelley mischaracterizing her
  statements as disparaging remarks.

  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness attempted to clarify what he called a cheap shot from Council
  Member Schlicht at the last meeting. He drew attention to page 8 of the Minutes where
  Council Member Schlicht commented on the check that was written to his business, Kwik
  Kopy Printing. She is quoted as saying that her purpose in bringing the item forward was
  to “stop the Council's positions from being exploited for self-enrichment.” Mayor Pro
  Tem Leckness stated that Council Member Schlicht was fully aware that the $250 check
  to Kwik Kopy printing was paid in November 2009, months before he became a City
  Council Member. He asked Council Member Schlicht to break away from the
  stranglehold of cynicism so the city can move forward in the positive direction that it
  deserves.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to approve the
  Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of September 7, 2010, as amended.

  Amendment: final Minutes will reflect that Assistant City Manager/Director of
  Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein was absent.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

5.  Quarterly Check Registers and Quarterly Cash Receipts Report - Fourth Quarter
  of FY 2009-10

  Council Member Schlicht thanked Irwin Bornstein for supplying this comprehensive
  report. In viewing it, the public can see all of the city's fiscal year-end spending.

City Council Minutes  6  September 20, 2010
   Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to receive
  and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

6.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - For The Year Ended
  June 30, 2010 (Preliminary-Unaudited)

  Mayor Kelley announced that this report identifies the city’s general fund revenues and
  general fund reserves. She noted that Council Member Schlicht and her friends have
  questioned the figures she used in her candidate statement and here are the same figures
  in black and white. The city’s total discretionary reserves at the end of Fiscal Year 2009-
  10 were $25.8 million. The quarterly financial reports are prepared after the books are
  examined at the close of the quarter and residents should be aware that the city has just
  about $26 million in discretionary reserves. She also reiterated that she pulled this item
  from the consent calendar since her figures have been questioned.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

18.  Ordinance Update of Chapter 11.16 of Title 11 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code
  to prevent Commercial Use of Residential Property; Particularly Prohibiting
  Marijuana Grow Houses

  Council Member Schlicht encouraged her colleagues to reverse their vote. She stated that
  laws are already in effect to prohibit marijuana grow houses and commercial uses in
  residential dwellings. She further expressed concern that this will be a foundation for
  eliminating in-home businesses in the future.

  City Attorney Curley described that the intent of the ordinance is not to do anything to
  prohibit home based businesses. Rather, the ordinance is designed to protect
  neighborhoods from people who don’t live in a single family property and instead turn it
  into a commercial business, most commonly a grow house.

City Council Minutes  7  September 20, 2010
   Carl T. Raff, M.V.: expressed concern about the ordinance and asked the Council
  Members to vote against it.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to adopt
  Ordinance 10-283 Amending Chapter 11.16 of Title 11 of the Mission Viejo Municipal
  Code.
  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

21.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

22.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

23.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Attorney’s Report

24.  Review of San Jose Revolving Door Ordinance

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the report.

  By consensus, the City Council received and filed the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Council Member Schlicht

26.  Preserving the Master Plan

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

City Council Minutes  8  September 20, 2010
   The following spoke in opposition to the proposed ordinance: Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.;
  Dan Avery, M.V.; Helen Workun, M.V.; Kate Keena, M.V.; Dennis O’Connor, M.V.;
  Sherri Butterfield, M.V.; Marion Butterfield, M.V.; and Rick Sandzimier.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht to direct the City Attorney to create an
  ordinance giving our voters the right to ratify or reject council approval on major changes
  to zoning or the City’s major planning documents that: increase housing density on a
  parcel when not mandated by state law; change any open space land use to allow any
  other land use; change any recreation land use to allow any other land use except open
  space; converts commercial zoning for residential use or a mix of residential and
  commercial use.

  The motion died for lack of a second.

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg announced that this Saturday is the annual Readers’ Festival. There will
be quite a few well known authors and it should be a great day out at the Community Center.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

25.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma inquired about the temporary moratorium related to the Casta del Sol
golf course and asked when it expired.

City Attorney Bill Curley replied that the two-year ordinance was put in place as an interim
zoning tool to allow deliberation and analysis of open space parcels. The ordinance has lapsed
and therefore the General Plan and zoning guidelines are the city’s regulatory tools at this time.
Mr. Curley noted that once that two-year window of time was exhausted, the Council could not
adopt something substantially similar.

RECESS

At the hour of 8:38 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:45
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  9  September 20, 2010
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

Council Member Schlicht

27.  "Aunt Lu"

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to direct the
  Community Services Commission to evaluate the concept of naming a park, ballfield or
  scoreboard after "Aunt Lu."

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

Council Member Schlicht noted that the City Council open space zoning moratorium expired in
January of 2009. She found it quite interesting that she was no longer allowed to discuss the
ordinance this evening yet the dialogue continued during Council Member Ledesma’s comments.
The purpose of the moratorium was to allow time for the City Council to do something further
and Council Member Schlicht stated that no one did anything. She announced that she brought
forward a proposal similar to Measure D in order to allow the City Attorney to fix the problems
associated with that measure. She also discussed her proposal for a revolving door ordinance.
She stated that she did not intend to embarrass Mayor Pro Tem Leckness but she doesn’t want
commissioners and committee members taking advantage of their positions. Council Member
Schlicht announced that she attended the Teen Challenge annual barbecue where she heard
testimony from young men whose lives were devastated by drugs and alcohol. With the help of
the program, they were able to turn their lives around and are now helping others find their way
out of the endless maze of addiction. She encouraged those who have a loved one in trouble to
seek out Teen Challenge. Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with racial undertones in
Commissioner Robert Bruchmann’s correspondence. She stated that it is more than evident that
Mr. Bruchmann classifies people and she asked how a commissioner can be removed or their
resignation requested. Addressing Mayor Kelley’s comments from the meeting of September 7,
Council Member Schlicht stated that she did not make disparaging statements about the city and
she challenged anyone to find such a remark. She suggested that Mayor Kelley is not to use the
city’s official Minutes as her personal ballot statement or to use the dais for hyperbole. Council
Member Schlicht feels that she has always championed the citizens of the city and she stated that
they make this city an outstanding community in which to live and raise a family.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury expressed concern with the public speakers earlier this evening who threw
out righteous indignation because there are web sites supporting candidates that they don’t like.

City Council Minutes  10  September 20, 2010
 He noted that he has served on the City Council for six years and every level of disparaging
remark has been aimed at him. He also pointed out that there are currently election signs posted
throughout the city showing Mayor Kelley’s and Mayor Pro Tem Leckness’ names with a slash
through them. He stated that the city has dealt with a lot over the past year between a recall
election, a special election and a revisit of Measure D tonight. The small group of people
supporting these things are running around acting holier than thou. Council Member Ury
reflected on the City’s Investment Advisory Commissioner whose home is in financial distress as
the same person who has spent three years disparaging every decision the City Council makes.
He stated that this individual stood on street corners with a megaphone announcing what terrible
people he and his colleagues are, the Commissioner’s candidate statement blasts everybody who
has ever been associated with the city, yet when the same person has financial troubles, no one is
supposed to touch that. Council Member Ury noted that there is another candidate who refuses
to reveal his street address and he thinks that’s an issue that people should know about. He
stated that it’s just a little bit on the politically immature side to think that these discussions and
attacks can only go one way. Council Member Ury expressed confidence in some of the
candidates whom he feels would do a great job if they are elected or re-elected to the City
Council. He noted that the critics who have spent years pounding on him and his colleagues
should expect them to respond in kind. He also commented on Council Member Schlicht’s
statement that she didn’t intend to slam Mayor Pro Tem Leckness. He asked her to be honest
and take her shots but not to deny them. Council Member Ury concluded his comments by
encouraging residents to attend the Readers’ Festival this Saturday. There were over 5,000
attendees last year and he believes there will be even more visitors to this 2nd annual event.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness acknowledged Council Member Ledesma who is nearing the end of
twelve years of dedicated service to the City of Mission Viejo. He also announced that resident
Joanie O’Neil who owns Mission Viejo Florist was invited by President Obama to attend a small
business forum with representatives from around the country. President Obama spoke to the
group and they brainstormed about business concerns and developed new ideas. He was pleased
to learn that Mission Viejo Florist was one of only 100 businesses invited to participate in the
forum and Ms. O’Neil has now returned home to share the information with other local
businesses.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley announced that she is sorry Council Member Schlicht doesn’t like for her to give
positive comments about the city but she can’t help herself. Mission Viejo is a fantastic place to
live and singing the city’s praises is part of who she is. She is grateful for the environment the
city provided for her to raise her three children and she hears the same from residents all the
time. Mayor Kelley encouraged residents to keep their eyes open for the new City Outlook.
There is a lot of good information about upcoming events including the Readers’ Festival and
Santa’s Workshop in December. She reiterated that when she removed item 6 from the Consent
Calendar, she wanted to share the good news that the city’s discretionary reserves are at $25.8
million which is 54% of general fund revenues. It is a good solid quarterly financial report and

City Council Minutes  11  September 20, 2010
 virtually the same information that was presented to the City Council with the quarter ending
March 31. Mayor Kelley announced that she was pleased to attend a memorial ceremony on
September 11, 2010, provided by one of the local Cub Scout troops from Pack 703. The scouts
held a flag raising ceremony at city hall in honor of the victims of 9/11 and she was very proud
of the Cub Scouts for organizing the nice, informal gathering. Mayor Kelley thanked members
of the community who turned out for the blood drive that she hosted on September 9 to honor the
victims and heroes of 9/11. Also, on September 10, 2010, she and the City Manager met with
Supervisory Pat Bates to talk about a variety of issues including the interest the city may have in
obtaining a portion of the County’s property for a dog park off Olympiad Road. Mayor Kelley
discussed her attendance at the League of Cities conference where she spent a lot of time in
workshops and study sessions and she came away with good information. She also found it to be
a great opportunity to network with leaders from other cities. Finally, Mayor Kelley encouraged
residents to attend the Readers’ Festival on Saturday, September 25, 2010, from 10:00 a.m. to
5:00 p.m. at the Community Center and Oso Viejo Park and she reminded residents to mark their
calendars for the annual Walk Against Drugs on Saturday, October 23, 2010.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:13 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Monday, October 4, 2010 at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 4, 2010

City Council Minutes  12  September 20, 2010
